claims: 22.45B XRP across 701 attributed wallets and 24 exchanges; daily wallet reads are described as rippled account_info reads around 08:00 UTC.
Same-wallet change: -161.1M XRP over seven days and -12.7M over 30 days.
Tracked exchange holdings include cold storage, omnibus/customer balances and approximately 487.9M XRP of non-customer reserves such as cbXRP and Binance-Peg.
ETF/index holdings: approximately 1.1966B XRP and $1.51B AUM; weekly net flow +3.39M XRP for October 26–30; October 30 flow approximately -49.9K XRP.
RLUSD supply split: $707.4M on XRPL and $1.71B on Ethereum, approximately $2.42B combined, as of November 1.
18 XRPL tokenized-asset entries represent approximately $4.33B, of which the tracker classifies $276M as distributed transferable float and $4.06B as registry-style issuer notionals.
methodology: Exchange balances are attributed wallet balances read from XRPL; the tracker describes them as a floor because unattributed wallets are omitted.
RLUSD XRPL supply is described as rippled gateway_balances on the canonical issuer account; Ethereum supply is described as contract totalSupply().
ETF data is sourced from issuer pages, with per-fund as-of dates and source-status distinctions.
limitations: Attributed exchange-wallet balances are not customer-owned balances, executable order-book depth or tradable float.
The 7-day wallet movement may include exchange wallet migrations to unattributed addresses; it does not prove customer withdrawals.
GXRP flow data is excluded where the tracker reports a scrape gap; some historical rows are reconstructed; BITW is an index product with rebalancing.
The ETF average-cost and unrealized-loss figures are tracker estimates, not issuer-reported investor cost bases.
RWA registry notionals are not equivalent to transferable securities or capital locked in liquid markets.
The tracker is not the issuer and its live on-chain reads were not independently retrieved in this run.

claims: The hub displays 14,830,761 all-time x402 payments/volume-settled events and $48,329.34 USD value settled.
The hub displays 183 registered merchants and 5,318 live services.
The displayed four-week average weekly USD settlement value is approximately $3,875.
The facilitator supports XRP and issued assets including RLUSD and USDC.
The facilitator describes itself as non-custodial and says the payer signs the XRPL Payment transaction.
limitations: The dashboard is operated by the facilitator whose activity it measures; it is not an independent audit.
The merchant directory page displayed 178 merchants while the home dashboard displayed 183 registered merchants.
Recent settlement cards displayed an Unverified label despite the page's general verified-before-settlement description.
The displayed event count is not established as an equal count of unique XRPL ledger transactions; batch settlement can aggregate multiple logical payments.
The USD value is small relative to the event count and does not establish material XRP spot demand.

claims: The XRPL Exact scheme uses payer-presigned Payment transactions; the facilitator submits the signed transaction.
The payer pays the XRPL transaction fee.
XRP and issued assets such as RLUSD are supported.
The documented verification checks include network binding, destination, amount, expiry, invoice binding and policy checks.
The documentation describes invoice binding as a replay-prevention requirement.
limitations: Documentation establishes intended protocol behavior, not that every observed dashboard payment passed independent verification.
SourceTag 804681468 is shown as a default in the documentation and should not be treated as a unique identity proof by itself.

claims: Coinbase contributed the x402 protocol to the Linux Foundation for open, vendor-neutral governance.
Circle, Coinbase, Ripple and t54 Labs are listed among the x402 Foundation members.
Ripple states that it is building XRPL support for x402 using XRP and RLUSD.
Circle states that x402 and USDC support agent payments.
limitations: Membership and protocol contribution do not establish commercial exclusivity, joint market-making, XRP purchases or shared treasury activity.
The Foundation announcement does not publish participant-level payment volumes.

claims: Arc launched with USDC as its gas asset and a founding validator cohort including SBI Group.
Coinbase and Binance are listed among exchange participants; Aave and Morpho are listed among lending integrations.
Circle states USDC accounted for 98.8% of agent-driven transaction volume.
SBI Group's chairman says SBI intends to contribute to Arc operation/governance and leverage USDC and JPYSC.
Circle says SBI VC Trade became Japan's first and only USDC distributor in March 2025.
limitations: The 98.8% claim does not specify the denominator, period, chain coverage or whether volume means count or monetary value in the announcement.
Arc participation is not proof that all listed participants are validators or that they route XRP through Arc.
Company launch claims are not independent measurements of realized settlement volume.

limitations: Native issuance establishes availability, not material supply, liquidity, trading volume or XRP demand.

sources.publisher: SBI Holdings and Project Trinity participants
claims: Project Trinity phase 1 and phase 2 operational verification were completed.
Phase 2 ran from April through September 2026 and tested DvP settlement for security-token secondary-market transfers.
The settlement asset was a third-type electronic payment instrument issued by Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation in the form of specified trust beneficiary rights.
Progmat and Datachain supplied cross-chain technology; TISI and Fireblocks supplied the stablecoin infrastructure.
Participants included SBI Securities, Daiwa Securities, SBI R3 Japan, Osaka Digital Exchange, BOOSTRY, Progmat, Datachain and SBI VC Trade.
limitations: This was a proof-of-concept/operational verification, not proof of production settlement volume.
The announced settlement asset was not identified as XRP, RLUSD or USDC.
Participation by SBI affiliates does not establish a direct SBI Holdings treasury position in XRP.

limitations: Group ownership and fintech business description do not establish that SBI Ripple Asia itself holds, trades or uses XRP.
